### English source — DO NOT EDIT

<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_BEGIN -->
* Foreign rights licensing is the process of allowing a publisher in one country to legally publish and distribute a book that was originally published in another country.
* This allows authors to reach a wider audience and increase their financial success.
* Publishers will typically purchase the rights to publish a book in a specific language or territory.
* The process can be complex and may involve legal and financial considerations.
* Foreign rights licensing can also promote cultural exchange and understanding by making books from different countries more widely available.
* The publisher that buys the rights will translate the book into their local language and distribute it in their country.
* The publisher that owns the rights will get a percentage of the revenue generated by the sales of the translated book.
* The author of the book will also get a percentage of the revenue generated by the sales of the translated book.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_END -->
